sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Staff Advisors
sections.text:
Although it is your responsibility to know the requirements of your major and to complete those requirements on time, advisors are here to help you navigate through your academic career and get the most out of your time at UC Davis.
It is encouraged that you meet with an advisor once a year to review your efforts, especially once you begin your upper-division courses.
In addition to your Math Department advisors, we also suggest that you periodically consult the Undergraduate Education and Advising (UEA) advisors in the College of Letters and Science.
The hours listed below correspond to our two staff advisors' scheduled hours. Please be prepared to wait in the virtual/in-person waiting room for drop-in's as hours can be busy at times. Drop-in advising is done on a first-come, first-serve basis. Our advisors do not have any Summer Drop-In Hours. Please email studentservices@math.ucdavis.edu if you have any questions regarding staff advising.
Marji LeGrand, Undergraduate & Graduate Supervisor legrand@ucdavis.edu
Dawn Chandler, Undergraduate Coordinator dchandler@ucdavis.edu

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > General Tips From Our Peers
sections.text:
If you need to take both ECS32A and ENG6, take ECS32A first! Python (which is taught in ECS32A), is often viewed as the beginner coding language and MATLAB (which is taught in ENG6) is much easier to grasp once you are familiar with Python.
Taking MAT 145 before MAT 135A can better your understanding of the material being taught in the course (and some professors expect you to have taken 145 first!)
When deciding which of the 128 series courses you want to take, look back at your experience in 21C, 22A, and 22B. 128A will align with ideas and topics taught in 21C, 128B with ideas from 22A, and 128C with ideas from 22B.
We recommend scheduling courses from the MAT 128 series and MAT 150 series in your 4th year because they require more extensive knowledge from previous classes and can be more difficult.
For LMOR majors, we recommend scheduling MAT 168 and MAT 170 in your 4th year, following the completion of the MAT 170 prerequisite course (MAT 167 or MAT 128B or ECS 130).
Find a study group! It can be intimidating at times to find classmates you are comfortable working with, but having these connections can make or break your experience in a math class.
Utilize office hours and the TAs! Regardless of how intimidating they may be, it is their job to help you learn the material. They expect you to have questions on new material so if you have one, ask!
Need more individualized help? Many on-campus resources offer tutoring in lower division math courses (Stem Cafe, Academic Success Center, and the Department’s Calc Room to name a few). Need help in an upper division course? Many of our very own grad students offer tutor services to undergrads (for a fee).

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Mandatory Advising
sections.text: Interacting with advisors can help you clarify your objectives and achieve your goals. Choose one of the topics below to learn more about advising you'll need in order to meet College requirements, and when.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > First Year Transfer Students (Winter Quarter)
sections.text: Mandatory advising for new transfer students occurs in Winter Quarter. The goal of mandatory advising for new transfer students is to ensure that you have the opportunity to meet your major advisor, develop an academic plan for your major classes, discuss helpful resources, and address any questions or concerns you may have.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > First Year Transfer Students (Winter Quarter) > Important Dates
sections.text: Your mandatory advising hold will go into effect on March 15. It is important that you follow all mandatory advising steps so that your registration is not blocked after that date. Prior to March 15, you will be able to add, change, and drop classes as usual.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > First Year Transfer Students (Winter Quarter) > How to Release Your Hold
sections.text:
Step 1:
Make your plan
This can be saved as a draft in OASIS (located in the Academic Plan section of "Forms & Petitions").
Not sure what major requirements you still need to complete? Start by check out the "Degree Worksheets" section of OASIS for all your remaining major classes. You can also find PDF versions of the Degree Worksheets on the math major pages.
Step 2: Meet with an academic advisor in the Math Department to review your academic plan, discuss campus resources, etc. You can either meet with Dawn or Marji (your staff advisors).
Book your appointment

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Second Year Sophomore Students (Spring Quarter)
sections.text: Mandatory advising for second year students occurs in Spring Quarter. The goal of mandatory advising for second year students is to ensure that you are making good progress towards your major requirements, connect you with helpful resources, and answer questions that you may have.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Second Year Sophomore Students (Spring Quarter) > How to Release Your Hold
sections.text:
Update your plan here
Update your academic plan in OASIS to reflect plans for next 3 quarters. This can be saved as a draft in OASIS (in the Academic Plan section of "Forms & Petitions").
Start by checking out the "Degree Worksheets" section of OASIS for all your remaining major classes. You can also find PDF versions of the Degree Worksheets on the math majors page.
Step 2: Meet with an academic adviser in the Math Department to review your academic plan, discuss campus resources, etc. You can either meet with Dawn or Marji (your staff advisors).
To meet with Dawn or Marji, please schedule an appointment.
Step 3 (optional):
It is recommended that you create yourself a resume to begin looking for job and/or research opportunities. The ICC has great workshops to attend, take advantage of your campus resources here at UCD.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Fourth Year Seniors (Fall Quarter)
sections.text: Mandatory advising for seniors occurs in Fall Quarter. The goal of mandatory advising for seniors is to ensure that you are on track to graduate, plan for your transition out of college, and plan your next steps towards your professional goals.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Fourth Year Seniors (Fall Quarter) > Important Dates
sections.text: Your mandatory advising hold will go into effect on December 15. It is important that you follow all mandatory advising steps so that your registration is not blocked after that date. Prior to December 13 you will be able to add, change, and drop classes as usual.

sections.heading: Math Department Advising > Fourth Year Seniors (Fall Quarter) > How to Release Your Hold
sections.text:
Make your plan here
Not sure what major requirements you still need to complete? Start by check out the "Degree Worksheets" section of OASIS for all your remaining major classes. You can also find PDF versions of the Degree Worksheets on the math major pages.
After you complete the steps above, your hold will be lifted within 2 weeks.
